classification.difficultyReason: Read the duration of one repeating cycle from a supplied position–time graph.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows the motion of a swinging pendulum and its graph.

What is the period of this graph?

spec.description: Seven positions of one pendulum suspended from a fixed support, symmetric about the central vertical position. An outward double-ended curved arrow connects the negative and positive displacement directions.
spec.mathematics: Equal string lengths and symmetric angular positions represent the motion. Diagram coordinates are illustrative and carry no numerical length or angle givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All seven positions, directional arrows and displacement labels are permanent question givens.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, wide graph below the prompt and illustration
spec.description: Position–time graph from 0 to 30 seconds with one-second grid columns, time labels at every two seconds from 2 to 28, and six complete sinusoidal cycles.
spec.mathematics: The curve begins at zero rising, repeats every five seconds, and ends at zero rising. Drawing ordinates encode the source proportions only; no numerical vertical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied curve, grid, axes and time labels remain visible. No period annotation or supplied answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses zero rising at $t=0\text{ s}$ and again at $t=5\text{ s}$. These points mark one complete cycle.

$$\begin{align*}T&=5-0\\T&=5\text{ s}\end{align*}$$
